$comment: RELEASE-INTEGRITY POLICY — the set of checks that MUST be green, for the EXACT
commit being deployed, before any production rollout starts.
Why workflows are pinned by numeric `id` and not by `name`: a workflow's display
name is just a `name:` line in a YAML file that any commit can change. Pinning the
name means a commit that renames a cheap always-green workflow to 'Production CI'
satisfies the gate while the real CI is red or deleted. The numeric id is minted by
GitHub per workflow FILE PATH and cannot be claimed by another file.
`path` is asserted too, as a second, independent key: the API reports the path each
run actually executed. id+path disagreeing means the pinned id no longer refers to
the file we think it does -> refuse rather than guess.
`requiredJobs` is the anti-gutting guard. Pinning only the workflow lets a commit
empty out ci.yml (delete every real step, keep a green no-op job) and still deploy.
The named jobs must EXIST in the run and be `success`; a deleted or renamed job is
a refusal, which forces the rename to be a deliberate, reviewed edit of this file.
Jobs deliberately NOT required: quality.yaml 'PR Size Check' (skipped by design on
advisory). Requiring an advisory job would make the gate lie about what blocks.
